title: Families, Housing, Community Services and Indigenous Affairs and Other Legislation Amendment (Further 2008 Budget and Other Measures) Bill 2008
portfolio: Families, Housing, Community Services and Indigenous Affairs

divisions.question: That this bill be now read a second time. That all words after “That” be omitted with a view to substituting the following words: “while not declining to give the bill a second reading the House: (1) notes the Coalition’s support for the provisions concerning the maternity immunisation allowance and child support; (2) notes the Coalition’s agreement to setting at 50 years of age eligibility for partner service pension for the partners of veterans who are in receipt of the equivalent of or less than the special rate but above the general rate disability, or who have at least 80 impairment points; (3) condemns the government’s stubborn determination to insist that from 1 January 2009 partners who are separated but not divorced from their veteran spouse and who have not reached the age for the age pension, will have their partner service pension eligibility cease 12 months after being separated or immediately if the veteran enters a marriage-like relationship”. That the words proposed to be omitted ( **Mrs Markus** ’s amendment) stand part of the question.

speeches.speaker: Kim Carr
speeches.brief: The bill restructures the maternity immunisation allowance into two payments ($121.65 each) for children aged 18 months–2 years and 4–5 years from January 2009, extends eligibility to overseas-adopted children under 16, ceases partner service pension for separated but not divorced partners under pension age, and makes minor child support amendments including care-level accuracy and departure prohibition orders for international parents.

speeches.speaker: Claire Moore
speeches.brief: The speaker presented the Standing Committee on Community Affairs report on the Families, Housing, Community Services and Indigenous Affairs and Other Legislation Amendment (Further 2008 Budget and Other Measures) Bill 2008 and ordered it printed.

speeches.speaker: Nigel Scullion
speeches.brief: The bill restructured the maternity immunisation allowance into two payments and extended it to overseas adopted children, made minor technical amendments to child support, and reduced partner service pension eligibility for separated partners of veterans, saving $40.6 million over four years; amendments were introduced to delay the commencement to July 2009 and exempt partners in unsafe domestic environments due to the veteran's accepted psychological condition.

speeches.speaker: Jan McLucas
speeches.brief: The speaker tabled a supplementary explanatory memorandum on government amendments to a 2008 budget bill and argued for establishing a no-fault vaccine injury compensation scheme like Quebec’s, referencing the Lapierre case. They also moved seven amendments to delay certain provisions to 1 July 2009 and exempt 87 people from being moved onto Newstart in the first year.

speeches.speaker: Russell Trood
speeches.brief: The government argued that no veteran would be worse off under the partner service pension changes, noting up to 580 separated partners and 390 veterans with mental conditions were potentially affected, with net savings of $28 million over four years. The opposition supported the government’s amendments but expressed concern that partners, not veterans, would bear the $28 million in cuts.

acts.title: Families, Housing, Community Services and Indigenous Affairs and Other Legislation Amendment (Further 2008 Budget and Other Measures) Act 2008
